findings.issue: The r1.1 typecheck gate log is a zero-byte file, so it attests nothing on its own; round 1's equivalent log records EXIT=0, which is the convention this file breaks. The tsc claim is carried indirectly by next build's 'Running TypeScript' step over a tree containing both r1.1-changed files, so the gate is satisfied but not by the artifact named for it.

The diff carries app/components/_aurora.scss (+34), which AC 10's confinement list does not name (app/lab/*, the new experiment components, the extracted riser and its two importers, tests). This is a defect in the bar's wording rather than the artifact: AC 2 explicitly sanctions _aurora.scss as one of the two shared sources, and the moved aurora-veil mixin is what keeps the three veil seats from forking.

The new lab-seat pin asserts a source-text regex for <AuroraRiser, so it proves textual presence rather than that the seat renders the riser; an unreachable or dead element would keep it green. The AC's literal bar (mutation-proven against deletion) is met, the idiom matches the route seat's existing pin, and runtime proof exists separately in the r1.1 toggle log, where the live layer child carries the riser module's own class.

Advisory, not blocking: at 375px the measured solid core falls to 51% for the rise and 41.8% for the sweep, against 79% at desktop frame scale, so the twelve columns read as one smooth gradient. _aurora.scss's own comment says the stepped-then-softened combination IS the effect and that over-softening makes it a plain gradient. The shipped route transition degrades the same way at that width (62%) and did so before this ticket, and the build surfaced the measurement rather than quietly retuning the geometry, which is what the ticket asked for. Judgment for the human at the gate.

Advisory: the reduced-motion still for the sweep parks the band at 70cqw, so the only visible remnant is the magenta tail of the spectrum against the window's clipped right edge, with the leading blue edge off screen. It is a real frame of the real run and it is not blank, so the AC is met, but it names its gesture noticeably less clearly than the riser's mid-growth still names the rise.

Reported ambiguity in the bar, not a defect in the artifact: the prompt builds the shipped route transition, while what the frame shows is a miniature site plus a gesture toggle, so an agent following it gets the effect but not the demo. AC 4's own words ('could build the effect from it') and the ticket's Decisions block both favor the artifact's reading; the registry field's phrasing ('recreate it') is what is loose. Worth tightening in the next lab ticket.

Simplicity: AuroraRiser's ms parameter is handed its own default at both call sites (the route seat passes SWEEP_MS, which is an alias of RISE_MS; the lab seat passes RISE_MS literally), so it is currently a knob with a single setting. It does document the contract that the seat owns the timer that swaps the page underneath, which is why this is advisory rather than a subtraction demand.
